svg.title: Ready to Move From Uber Black to Private Clients
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-private-black-car-gate-check; chapter number: 5; chart type: decision_tree; title: Ready to Move From Uber Black to Private Clients; subtitle: Four gates before taking direct bookings; caption: Operators who left the app agree Uber Black is a launchpad, not a business. Black Truck Mick grossed $15,070 in month one on a rented SUV, but only after pricing for the day and moving direct work to $100 an hour.; assumptions note: Gate order is an editorial sequence of practitioner gates; rates and the $300 daily break-even reflect one rented SUV costing $1,250 a week.; note: Fares and Frustrations (_UpXw8QDal8 @ 00:06:26), Business with Mide (4TzKcRuyrHY @ 00:00:44), Black Truck Mick (uODRGjORQF4 @ 00:10:28, uODRGjORQF4 @ 00:14:11), My Chauffeur Life (Y-1AudoR8JA @ 00:04:09), and Luxury Transportation Academy / Podcast (yg-RtCxYcG8 @ 00:09:02).; nodes: gate: G1; question: Are the TCP, permits, and airport credentials locked in?; pass next: G2; fail action: Hold launch; operating without the TCP is illegal and the wrong airport permit or credential means lost bookings.; gate: G2; question: Does pricing cover the day, not just the ride?; pass next: G3; fail action: Reprice; Black Truck Mick needed $300 a day to cover a rented SUV and admits $40 for six riders was too little.; gate: G3; question: Is a weekly reserve funded with every expense tracked?; pass next: G4; fail action: Build the reserve first, before a luxury repair costing thousands parks the car for weeks.; gate: G4; question: Do reservations live in a CRM or booking system?; pass next: Take direct work at $100 an hour, $80 for affiliates, fed by hotel concierges, event planners, and corporate assistants.; fail action: Pull bookings out of WhatsApp and text threads, where nine times out of 10 they get lost.

text.title: Ready to Move From Uber Black to Private Clients
text.tspan: Ready to Move From Uber Black to Private Clients

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Are the TCP, permits, and airport credentials locked in?; pass next: G2; fail action: Hold launch; operating without the TCP is illegal and the wrong airport permit or credential means lost bookings.

gate: G2; question: Does pricing cover the day, not just the ride?; pass next: G3; fail action: Reprice; Black Truck Mick needed $300 a day to cover a rented SUV and admits $40 for six riders was too little.
gate: G3; question: Is a weekly reserve funded with every expense tracked?; pass next: G4; fail action: Build the reserve first, before a luxury repair costing thousands parks the car for weeks.

gate: G4; question: Do reservations live in a CRM or booking system?; pass next: Take direct work at $100 an hour, $80 for affiliates, fed by hotel concierges, event planners, and corporate assistants.; fail action: Pull bookings out of WhatsApp and text threads, where nine times out of 10 they get lost.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order is an editorial sequence of practitioner gates; rates and the $300 daily break-even reflect one rented SUV costing $1,250 a week.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Gate order is an editorial sequence of practitioner gates; rates and the $300 daily break-even reflect one rented SUV
